description: Frozen local operating protocol matrix for the current Q/F split, seed budgets, and narrow repair-note sanity workflow, rechecked after fast-default hardening, stress-target reduction, the target-specific hypothesis probes, the extreme-tail closeout / split-target confirmation pass, and now locked as the local baseline snapshot / regression guard reference.

explore.rule: Use budget-first F for quick local loops.
explore.stop_label_semantics: accept_fast_exploratory = stop on F for the quick loop; if route quality becomes sensitive, switch to Q instead of extending F.
explore.final_confirm_recommendation: If route quality is sensitive or an anti-case/corridor-like instance is plausible, switch to Q on 8-10 seeds.
explore.rationale: Post-hardening recalibration plus the latest extreme-tail contour pass kept F useful for quick local iteration, but the best nearby contour only nudged anti-case p95 while worsening max tail, so the budget-first note still cannot close corridor-like extremes.

compare.rule: Run only the current paired Q/F compare; do not search new candidates here.
compare.stop_label_semantics: accept_fast_exploratory = F is still fine for the paired exploratory read; reject_early / require_q_confirm = stop trying to rescue F and move to Q.

rescue_target.note: Rescue-target-only rows are the one place where paired 5 seeds still pay off.

anti_case.note: Anti-case suspicion goes straight to the Q final path.

compare.final_confirm_recommendation: If anti-case suspicion or quality sensitivity matters, skip F rescue and use Q on 8-10 seeds.
compare.rationale: The latest same-budget tradeoff probe left the compare ladder structurally unchanged: rescue-target-only ambiguity is still the only place where the 5-seed step earns its keep, while anti-case-aware work still closes more honestly on Q because late cleanup remains the weak point.

final.rule: Use quality-first Q for quality-sensitive or anti-case-aware final decisions.
final.stop_label_semantics: require_q_confirm = this mode intentionally bypasses F rescue and closes with Q confirmation.
final.final_confirm_recommendation: Run Q directly on 8-10 seeds; do not try to rescue F in quality-sensitive or anti-case-aware finals.
final.rationale: Even after the latest same-budget tradeoff probe, TSP still closes on a descriptive Q/F split rather than a promoted numeric tolerance rule.

explore.rule: Use budget-first F for quick HV-first exploratory reads.
explore.stop_label_semantics: accept_fast_exploratory = F is good enough for the cheap HV-first loop; it is not the final safety call.
explore.final_confirm_recommendation: If you need spread / Pareto safety, switch to Q on 8-10 seeds.
explore.rationale: Post-hardening recalibration plus the latest spread-vs-joint split confirmation kept fast ZDT1 runs useful for exploratory HV reads, but timing-only probes still did not close the joint safety risk and spread still looks more population/generation-sensitive.

compare.rule: Run only the current paired Q/F compare; keep HV and safety in the same read.
compare.stop_label_semantics: accept_fast_exploratory = F is still fine for the paired exploratory read; require_q_confirm = safety-sensitive work should move to Q.
compare.final_confirm_recommendation: If the decision is safety-sensitive, skip the hopeful ladder and use Q on 8-10 seeds.
compare.rationale: The latest spread-vs-joint split confirmation kept the same shape: F still works at 3 paired seeds for exploration, but the safety-aware closing read still snaps back to Q because the remaining spread failures are not timing-only and joint failures are not cleanly timing-only either.

final.rule: Use quality-first Q when spread / Pareto safety is part of the final call.
final.stop_label_semantics: require_q_confirm = this mode intentionally closes with the safety-aware Q confirm instead of letting F through on HV alone.
final.final_confirm_recommendation: Run Q directly on 8-10 seeds for final safety-aware ZDT1 decisions.
final.rationale: Cooldown=3 still gives the most honest budget-first envelope, but HV can still look acceptable before spread / Pareto safety settle, and the timing-only probes did not remove that closing risk.

sanity.rule: Keep the broad default parked and sanity-check the narrow repair_only note only.
sanity.stop_label_semantics: repair_note_stable = the narrow repair_only note still holds; if the family looks tight-capacity or borderline, extend the sanity check to 5 seeds.

tight_capacity_small.note: Tight-capacity rows earn the longer sanity check.

sanity.final_confirm_recommendation: Use 3 seeds for the narrow repair_only sanity check, and extend to 5 only for tight-capacity or otherwise borderline rows.
sanity.rationale: The freeze recheck kept knapsack without a broad default; the only honest rule remains a narrow repair-note sanity path.

control.rule: Keep OneMax as a fixed control-only problem.
control.stop_label_semantics: control_stable = the control read is already flat enough that a larger sequential ladder adds no value.
control.final_confirm_recommendation: One seed control is enough; there is no reason to spend a larger ladder here.
control.rationale: The freeze recheck kept OneMax as a control surface, not a place for a richer local operating protocol.
